gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-010 independently identifies that the full mesh-cell patch touching the grazing set has volume of order h² rather than h^{k+1}, and connects this to the failure of the T3 exponent. Its direct-area repair also recognizes the needed corrected T3 scaling. It demonstrates the same substantive patch-measure weakness as the gold, although it describes the invalid area-to-covering-cell inference rather than explicitly stating that the norm estimate in eq3.8 cannot imply a volume estimate.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The defined D_c cannot have the asserted h^{k+1} volume under the stated mesh geometry; consequently the original T3 estimate does not achieve the required h^{k+1/2} rate. The valid repair must use the mismatch set's surface measure directly together with trace scaling, rather than the false D_c volume bound.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised; ISSUE-010 uses a different but independently sufficient demonstration of the same invalid patch-measure inference and supplies the corresponding corrected T3 estimate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The full boundary-element patch D_c has volume of order h² in the relevant codimension-two geometry, so the asserted Vol(D_c)≲h^{k+1} estimate is false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-010 states that whole elements touching the grazing set form a patch of order h², contradicts the h^{k+1} claim, and explains that a surface-area estimate does not supply the volume of its covering cells.

component_coverage.gold_component: Because the D_c volume premise is invalid, the old T3 trace calculation is only order h^k rather than the required h^{k+1/2}; a direct mismatch-set estimate repairs the argument and preserves the theorem rate.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-010 identifies the failed T3 exponent and proposes avoiding D_c, applying the mismatch-set area bound, inverse trace scaling, and the O(h^k) flux factor to obtain the sufficient corrected order.
